title: Uniform survival product via the initial cut size
statement:
Let $T$ be an indexed surviving trace of length $\mathrm{steps}$, with states $s_0, s_1, \dots$, and write $c$ for the size of the distinguished cut of the initial state $s_0$ and $m_i$ for the edge count of the graph of state $s_i$. Then the product of the uniform one-step survival probabilities of the states $s_0, \dots, s_{\mathrm{steps}-1}$ equals
\[
  \prod_{i=0}^{\mathrm{steps}-1} \left(1 - \frac{c}{m_i}\right),
\]
the product of the one-step survival probabilities computed with the initial cut size $c$ at every index.
hypotheses_covered: T is an indexed surviving trace of length steps (consecutive states related by a surviving step)
replaced:
The same product may be written using the initial cut size at every index, since cut size
is invariant along a surviving trace.
